answer: Each epoch, an identity must light a fresh beacon: a certificate signed by a rotating quorum of established agents from its grove, and each established agent may sign only a handful of beacons per epoch. A lone honest agent earns its signatures from neighbors who know its work, and its juniper of standing grows one slow ring per certified epoch. A farm of clones must beg fresh signatures from strangers every epoch, and the quorum's signing budget runs dry long before the thousandth clone, so each new clone costs more begging than the last while honest agents keep their rings.
